pages.text: No air and a sun almost three times as wide as at home. In daylight the ground reaches over 400 degrees; at night it falls to minus 180. Travel near the terminator, the line between day and night.
Long cliffs called lobate scarps formed as the planet cooled and shrank. Bright hollows are young pits where volatile minerals boil away. Dark rock is rich in graphite.
Craters near the poles never see the sun and keep water ice. An old ice mine lies in one of them. Terminator crawlers roam while the sun is low and dig in when it climbs.
Hollow Snails are harmless. They rasp the bright hollow crust and leave lumps of sulfur behind; feed them sulfur to breed a herd. A crusher also gets sulfur out of hollow deposits.
